embeds.title: 🔴 Exploit Available for New DirtyDecrypt Linux Root Escalation Flaw
embeds.description:
A proof-of-concept exploit is now available for DirtyDecrypt (also known as DirtyCBC), a local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Linux kernel's rxgk module. The V12 security team reported finding this flaw on May 9, 2026, though it was identified as a duplicate of a previously patched vulnerability. According to Will Dormann at Tharros, the details align with CVE-2026-31635, which was patched on April 25. The vulnerability affects Linux distributions with CONFIG_RXGK enabled, including Fedora, Arch Linux, and openSUSE Tumbleweed. Successful exploitation requires running a vulnerable kernel configuration and allows attackers to gain root access.
